content.value_statement: Teams need reliability targets that reflect real user impact. This skill helps define SLIs, SLOs, budgets, alerts, dashboards, and review steps.
actual_capabilities: Defines availability, latency, and durability SLIs from service metrics.
Helps choose SLO targets based on user expectations and business needs.
Calculates error budgets and maps budget levels to engineering actions.
Drafts Prometheus recording rules for SLI ratios and SLO compliance.
Creates multi-window burn rate alert patterns for budget consumption.
Outlines Grafana dashboard sections and recurring SLO review routines.
limitations: It provides implementation guidance, not automated deployment to monitoring systems.
Examples assume Prometheus-style metrics and Grafana-style dashboards.
It needs real service metrics and business targets for accurate SLO design.
It does not replace legal review for external SLA commitments.

use_cases.title: Define First Production SLOs
use_cases.description: Select user-facing SLIs, set practical targets, and document error budget policies for a critical service.

use_cases.title: Build Monitoring Rules
use_cases.description: Translate reliability goals into recording rules, burn rate alerts, and dashboard panels for operations teams.

use_cases.title: Run Reliability Reviews
use_cases.description: Use SLO compliance, budget status, incidents, and trends to guide planning and release decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Start an SLO Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a single service
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me define an initial SLO plan for this service. Ask for missing details about users, critical journeys, metrics, and business goals.

prompt_templates.title: Choose SLIs and Targets
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my service metrics and recommend availability, latency, and durability SLIs with realistic SLO targets and rationale.

prompt_templates.title: Design Error Budget Policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an error budget policy for a service with a monthly SLO window. Include thresholds, actions, owners, and review cadence.

prompt_templates.title: Implement Alerts and Reviews
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert these SLO goals into monitoring rules, burn rate alert strategy, dashboard sections, and weekly and monthly review steps.

output_examples.input: A checkout API needs a first SLO program.
output_examples.output: The skill would propose user-facing availability and latency SLIs, a realistic monthly target, an error budget policy, and review checkpoints.

output_examples.input: A team has noisy availability alerts.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend burn rate alert windows, budget-aware severities, and dashboard panels that separate urgent incidents from slow degradation.

output_examples.input: Leadership wants reliability tied to planning.
output_examples.output: The skill would outline monthly SLO reviews, budget status reporting, and decision rules for feature velocity and reliability work.

best_practices: Start with user-facing journeys before internal implementation metrics.
Use achievable SLOs and avoid targets that imply perfect reliability.
Review error budgets regularly and connect budget burn to release decisions.
anti_patterns: Defining SLOs without confirming the user experience they measure.
Alerting on every minor SLO change instead of using burn rate windows.
Setting reliability goals without an error budget policy or owner.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create SLIs, SLO targets, error budgets, alerting rules, dashboards, and review processes.

faq.question: Does it deploy Prometheus or Grafana configuration?
faq.answer: No. It provides examples and structure that engineers can adapt and deploy in their own systems.

faq.question: Can it help choose an SLO target?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides target selection using user expectations, business needs, current performance, and reliability cost.

faq.question: Does it cover error budgets?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains budget calculation, remaining budget, burn rate, and policy actions.

faq.question: Which monitoring style does it assume?
faq.answer: Most examples use Prometheus query patterns and Grafana dashboard concepts.

faq.question: Is it suitable for external SLA contracts?
faq.answer: It can inform reliability targets, but legal and customer commitments need separate review.
